text: What's the difference between a decision and an action item in meeting notes?

Before I email ari-example about partnering again, help me figure out what changed since we last spoke. Find our last substantive exchange and the reason things stalled, then check public sources for recent changes at their company, meadow-example. Separate what we actually know from guesses, and suggest whether to reopen the old thread or start fresh. Save the summary with my existing notes on them so I don’t have to reconstruct this next time.
Someone I’m meeting lists “fractional CFO” in their bio. What does that mean?

Need a competitive read on quarry-example before next week's planning session. Our product is spruce-example; the positioning notes and last quarter's battlecard should be in my knowledge base. What's changed in quarry-example's pricing, integrations, target customers, and product since that battlecard? Give me an updated comparison with links and a few concrete implications for our roadmap, not just a feature checklist. If pricing isn't public, say so rather than guessing.

Save https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762 to my reading notes, summarize the main ideas in plain English, and link it to whatever I already have on transformers and attention. Check for an existing note first so we don’t end up with two.

Friday catch-up time: review the waiting-on-me note in my knowledge base against this week's email and Teams messages. Close out anything that's resolved, add new promises I've made, and keep links to the evidence. Separate actual commitments from things where I just said I'd consider it, and show me what changed.

I owe a few customers replies but can't remember which ones. Check the last two weeks of threads involving harbor-example, birch-example, and lantern-example, including any internal Slack discussions where I volunteered to follow up. Draft a reply for each open obligation using the latest information in the thread, and flag anything you can't draft without an answer from me. Leave everything as drafts.

I've got 45 minutes before I log off for vacation. Find unanswered requests and unfinished promises from the past ten business days across my email and messages, then make me a realistic triage list: things I can finish now, things I should hand off, and things that can wait until I'm back on August 19. Check my calendar for deadlines, and draft handoff messages to the relevant teammates without sending them.

My dad gave me a drive dump of the family business, cedar-example, and it's a mess: scanned letters, contracts, spreadsheets, several folders called FINAL. It's under ~/Documents/business-archive. First show me what's in there and suggest what belongs in my knowledge base; wait for my approval before importing. Flag anything that looks like bank details, identity documents, or employee medical information so we can leave those out.
What's the difference between deduplicating old notes and merging them?

Can you track down where “93% of communication is nonverbal” actually came from? I need the original research, what it measured, and whether it supports using that line in a presentation. Give me a defensible replacement sentence with a citation if it doesn't.

The draft investor memo for cedar-example is at ~/Documents/cedar-example/investor-memo.md. Please check every external statistic and research citation, including whether the linked source actually supports the wording and whether a newer figure is available. Put the findings in a separate file with source links and suggested corrections; don't edit the memo yet. Flag anything you can only verify through a secondary source.

Before I repeat this at the board meeting, can you check mira-example's claim that our onboarding redesign cut churn by 18%? The claim is in last Thursday's meeting notes for harbor-example, and the monthly retention exports are in ~/work/harbor-example/metrics/. I can't tell whether she meant 18 percentage points or an 18% relative reduction, or whether she's comparing the same customer cohorts. Tell me what the data actually supports, note any missing evidence, and add a short sourced correction to the meeting note without deleting the original claim.

Can you draft my reply to mira-example in the latest email thread about the scope change for cedar-example? Read the whole thread and our meeting notes so I’m not agreeing to something we already ruled out. My sent emails should give you the tone—friendly, fairly blunt, no ‘hope this finds you well.’ I want to hold the original deadline but offer to drop the dashboard export. Leave it as a draft for me to review.

I’ve got a messy essay draft at ~/writing/drafts/being-small.md and comments from dev-example in the adjacent file. Can you turn it into something I’d actually put my name on? Compare it with the finished essays in that folder, figure out which feedback strengthens the argument versus just makes it more generic, and revise accordingly. Keep my odd little examples where they work, flag anything that needs evidence, and leave me a short note explaining the big cuts.

Please clean up the mess in my atlas-example vault. I've got duplicate people pages like sam-example and Sam-example (2), old project pages still marked active, and a bunch of links pointing to renamed meeting notes. Start with an inventory and a backup, merge only duplicates you're confident about, and keep all unique text and attachments. Update links and the main index, but put uncertain merges in a review list instead of guessing.

I'm meeting mira-example on Thursday to revisit our idea for a neighborhood tool library. Can you trace how our thinking has changed since January using our meeting notes, shared docs, and email threads? Separate things we actually agreed on from things one of us merely suggested, and put together a short catch-up brief with the unresolved questions.

Help me untangle my 'small teams, big output' idea. It's scattered through journal entries, conversations with nico-example and tess-example, and a few bookmarked articles. First figure out what claims I'm making, then look for examples in that material that support or contradict each claim. I want an argument outline I could turn into an essay, plus a short list of questions worth investigating next. Keep private anecdotes clearly marked so I don't accidentally publish them.
If a bug fix is backward-compatible, should its semantic version bump be patch or minor?

Review `feat/invite-expiry` against `main` before I merge it. This changes how team invitations expire in our Django app, and I'm especially worried about timezone handling and accepting the same invite twice. Trace the relevant callers, run the focused tests, and report concrete bugs with file/line references and severity. Don't edit anything.

Give PR #184 a proper security review in the current repo. It's adding PDF uploads to the customer portal for cedar-example. Follow an upload all the way from the HTTP endpoint through storage and download permissions, including what happens with malformed files and user-controlled filenames. Check the dependency changes too, and separate confirmed issues from things that need clarification.

I'm taking over `perf/search-cache-example` from jonah-example and don't trust the benchmark numbers in the PR description yet. Compare it with the merge base, reproduce the claimed speedup if you can, and look for stale results, cross-tenant cache leaks, and memory growth. Run whatever local checks are reasonable, but don't hit production services. Tell me what should block merge versus what can wait.

Please review the React/TypeScript changes on `release/settings-redesign-example` before this afternoon's merge. Check the diff against the existing API contracts, exercise the changed settings screens locally, and pay particular attention to keyboard navigation, failed saves, and unsaved edits when switching accounts. There are acceptance criteria in `docs/settings-acceptance.md`; use those to identify gaps, not just lint errors. End with a merge recommendation and the specific checks you couldn't complete.

Can you click through the signup and first-run setup on http://localhost:3000 in a real browser? Try both a normal new account and a few dumb inputs like a blank name, malformed email, and passwords that don’t match. Follow it all the way to creating the first workspace in harbor-example. Report what breaks with steps to reproduce and screenshots; don’t change the code yet.

Our Python API on Cloud Run is randomly returning 500s when customers upload PDFs. One happened around 14:20 UTC today for tenant cedar-example; the logs mention 'I/O operation on closed file.' Can you trace that request through the logs and code, fix the underlying issue, and add a regression test? Don't deploy anything yet.
What does 'connection refused' mean, and how is it different from a connection timeout?

Before I tell the team to build the weekly manager digest, sanity-check the idea against what we already know. Search my meeting notes and the feedback folder for complaints about missed updates versus notification overload, and look at the existing email jobs so we don’t promise data we can’t reliably assemble. marco-example wants every direct report’s activity included, but I’m worried that turns into a surveillance report rather than something useful. Draft a narrower proposal if the evidence supports one, with the main failure cases, the questions we still need to ask managers and employees, and what result would make us stop the experiment.

I need the landing page for lantern-example ready for a demo tomorrow. The copy and images are already in this repo, but the current page looks like a generic template. Give it a more editorial feel with stronger typography and a clearer signup section, without adding a bunch of animation. Build the changes, check desktop and mobile in the browser, and fix any awkward wrapping or overflow you find.

We added file uploads and URL previews to the Django service in dispatch-example, and I'd like a security pass before enabling them for everyone. Trace both features from the endpoints through storage and background jobs, then test whether an ordinary user can read someone else's uploads, upload dangerous content, or make the preview worker reach internal services. Use local fixtures only, no external targets. Fix confirmed issues and leave tests that demonstrate the protections.

We're getting complaints that POST /exports hangs, but I can't reproduce it with my tiny test account. There's a staging account called cedar-example with roughly 80,000 records that should be closer to reality. Trace the request through the API, database, and worker queue, reproduce the slowdown without sending any customer emails, and fix whatever is dominating the wait. Add a regression test and leave me a short note explaining what changed.
What's the difference between latency and throughput when people talk about a slow service?
What's the difference between a README and an API reference?

Can you track down the crash in the iOS app under ~/dev/trail-example? The latest crash logs are in ./crash-reports; users say it happens when they delete a saved route and immediately reopen it from Recents. Fix the underlying issue, add a regression test, and run whatever tests you can locally. Don't change the persistent store format unless it's actually necessary.

We got accessibility feedback from maya-example on the Android checkout in market-example: large text hides the Pay button, TalkBack reads the shipping options in a weird order, and some errors are only shown in red. Please reproduce these on an emulator, fix the checkout screens without redesigning them, and add whatever automated coverage makes sense. Leave me a quick summary of what still needs a manual device check.

We keep getting duplicate payment notifications from our webhook handler for cedar-example. Can you trace how incoming events get stored and processed, then make retries safe even if two copies arrive at once? There’s a Docker Compose setup for local testing. Add a regression test, and flag any migration or deployment ordering we’ll need before this goes live.

We’re adding team accounts to ledger-example, but the Postgres schema assumes every invoice belongs directly to a user. Look through the schema and the code that reads/writes invoices, propose a tenant-safe model, and implement the migrations and app changes. Existing users should each get a default team, and I need tests proving one team can’t see another team’s invoices.

The orders page in cart-example has gone from 200 ms to about 8 seconds since last week. Can you trace the query from the endpoint, inspect its execution plan against staging, and fix whatever is causing the slowdown? Use realistic filter combinations to check the improvement, and don’t add an index to production yet.

Move the staging API for cedar-example onto ECS Fargate. The app and Dockerfile are in this repo, and we already have an ECR repository and a Route 53 zone in the AWS account. Add the Terraform for an ALB, TLS, tasks, and the permissions it needs, then deploy and check that staging.cedar-example.com responds. Keep it to one small task for now and don't touch production.

The last deploy of orbit-example broke background jobs on our DigitalOcean Kubernetes cluster. Jobs sit pending, and I suspect the new node pool labels or resource requests. Compare the current deployment with the last working revision, check events and scheduling constraints, and fix staging first. Run a sample job through to completion, then give me the exact production change and rollback plan for approval.
What's the difference between macro-F1 and micro-F1 when evaluating a multiclass classifier?

Can you figure out which compounds in today's LC-MS run are actually worth following up? The peak table, blanks, pooled QCs and sample manifest are in /data/cedar-example/2026-04-12/. I want a shortlist of features enriched in the active fractions, with plausible identities where the mass and fragmentation support them—not confident names based on mass alone. Put the evidence and any quality concerns in a spreadsheet I can send to the chemistry team.

Harden the browser agent in cedar-example against instructions hidden in pages it reads. It still needs to research vendors and draft comparison tables, but page content mustn't be able to make it send emails or read local secrets. Add realistic attack cases, make the changes, and check that ordinary research tasks still work. Use fake credentials and a local test inbox only.

Can you add a reusable /release-check command to this agent for the lantern-example repo? Before each release I want it to compare changes against the last tag, run the relevant tests, flag migrations or new environment variables, and draft release notes. Have it stop and ask me if anything fails; it should never publish or push tags. Try it against the current branch so we can see whether the output is useful.

I've got a local Postgres database for orchard-example and want to ask this agent questions about it. Set up a read-only connection using an environment variable for the password, and give it enough schema context that it doesn't guess table names. Put sensible limits on query duration and result size. Test the setup with a couple of harmless questions, and make sure a request to update a row would be blocked.

How did the launch posts for lantern-example actually do? Pull the numbers from LinkedIn and X for the first 72 hours, compare them with our previous five launch posts, and check which links drove newsletter signups. I need a short readout that distinguishes reach from useful engagement, plus two concrete changes for the next launch. Note any tracking gaps rather than guessing.

Turn the recording and transcript from yesterday’s interview with mira-example into a week of social content for tidepool-example. Find four strong standalone ideas, draft an X thread and two LinkedIn posts, and suggest three short clips with timestamps and captions. Check quotes against the recording, and leave out the customer story she said was off the record.

Build me a list of 25 UK-based logistics software companies that look like good prospects for our usage-based billing product. Aim for 20–200 employees and look for evidence they sell an API or charge by transaction volume. Check our CRM for existing accounts before adding anything, and put the results in a CSV with website, fit rationale, source links, and likely buyer role. Flag uncertain matches rather than padding the list.

I've got a discovery call with mira-example at harbor-example tomorrow at 10. Pull together a brief from our past emails, meeting notes, and anything recent on their website: what they're trying to fix, who's involved, what we've promised, and what's still unanswered. Give me five useful questions and a suggested opening, but keep the actual call brief to one page.

Our runway model is in the attached spreadsheet, but I don’t trust the hiring assumptions anymore. For harbor-example, we have $1.8m cash as of June 30, monthly revenue of $92k, and three hires currently modeled to start in July. Build a revised base case with those hires starting in September, plus a downside case with revenue 20% below plan and collections delayed by 30 days. Check the existing formulas, keep bookings separate from cash receipts, and show when cash drops below $300k in each scenario. List any assumptions you had to make.

I need to write sam-example's midyear review by Friday. Pull together the goals, project updates, and our 1:1 notes from January through June, and draft a review with specific evidence for both impact and areas to improve. Separate my direct observations from feedback other people gave, point out anything that contradicts itself, and don't turn missing evidence into a negative assessment. Save the draft privately and give me a short list of gaps I should resolve with sam-example.

Get the first two weeks ready for priya-example, our new support lead starting September 14, 2026. Use the onboarding docs and team calendar to put together a realistic schedule, identify which accounts and permissions she'll need, and draft the access requests and welcome email. She's working UK hours and her manager, devon-example, is out on her second day, so make sure there's another person available to help. Save drafts, but don't create accounts or send anything until I approve.

We changed how workspace invites expire, and our help center is now contradicting itself. Compare the current behavior in the code with the invite-related articles, update the docs in the repo, and check the links and screenshots for anything else that needs replacing. Leave me a summary of what changed and anything you couldn’t verify.
What's the difference between first-response time and resolution time in customer support?

We agreed to add CSV imports to ledger-example, but the discussion is scattered across my notes from meetings with maya-example and otis-example. Pull those together with the existing API docs and write a spec covering the upload flow, field mapping, validation errors, duplicate handling, and what happens when an import partially fails. Separate actual decisions from assumptions, list the unanswered questions, and draft implementation tickets with acceptance criteria. Save everything under the project's planning folder.
Hey! Hope your day's going alright.
Thanks, that cleared it up perfectly.
